findings.message: When AMAX_BASE_URL is unset, `siteUrl()` quietly uses `http://localhost:3000`, even in production. This is also a second copy of the public-origin logic in `apps/web/lib/server.ts:112` `baseUrl()`, and that copy throws in production when the URL is missing (B4). The two can disagree: `server.ts:37` only requires AMAX_BASE_URL once DATABASE_URL is set, but AC-2 says the marketing page must render without a database. So a DB-less production deploy publishes localhost URLs and nothing flags it. Fix: build `siteUrl()` on the same rule as `baseUrl()` (fail in production when unset, and allow only loopback outside it), keep that rule in one place, and add a variant test (prod unset, prod set, dev unset).
findings.scenario: NODE_ENV=production, no DATABASE_URL, no AMAX_BASE_URL → GET / renders `<link rel=canonical href="http://localhost:3000/">` and an og:image on localhost, and /sitemap.xml lists `<loc>http://localhost:3000/</loc>`. Nothing errors.

findings.message: AC-3 requires every claim to match a shipped module and every unbuilt area to be marked "Coming". Only "People and payroll" is marked Coming, and that one is half wrong: hr and leave are shipped, payroll is not. These are presented as available but have no module: Finance and sales (contracts, billing milestones, expenses, Xero/QuickBooks/Business Central integration), Operations (IT assets and access, incidents, insights) and Delivery forecasts. The shipped modules are only allocations, compliance, delivery, hr, keyflow, learning, leave, notifications, presales and time. `tests/e2e/marketing.spec.ts:16` (`Coming` count = 1) locks in the wrong state. Fix: mark each unbuilt capability or area as Coming, or drop it, and have the test check the Coming set against `modules/*/module.ts`.
findings.scenario: A prospect reads "Finance and sales: Contracts, billing milestones, expenses… Integrates with Xero" with no Coming chip → no finance, expenses or accounting module exists in `modules/`.

findings.message: The matcher now skips the proxy for any path ending in .mp4, .webm or .vtt, not just for files under /marketing/. App page routes with those suffixes then skip the gate and the 035 page rate limit, the same hole that already exists for .png and .svg. Fix: exclude only `/marketing/` (or `public/` assets) by prefix, not by extension.
findings.scenario: Signed-in client repeatedly loads /delivery/x.webm → the (app) layout and catch-all page render server-side, and takeRate never runs.

findings.message: T5 is checked off, but the diff has no Lighthouse run (AC-8) and no visual snapshot. AC-10's check at the signed-out `/` only looks for the Main nav (landing.spec.ts:7); it does not check the top bar, search, chat launcher or profile. Either add these checks or mark them as not run in the change record.

AC-9 says the page takes its colours from `packages/ui` tokens. Instead, many brand and ticket colours are hard-coded (#A792FF, #53D6A1, #1D1B2E, the gradient stops in .mk-f.*, .mk-band, .mk-cta), so a token change won't reach the page. Use the token variables (e.g. --brand-violet, --brand-mint) or ticket-gradient tokens.
findings.scenario: Change --brand-violet in tokens.css → the hero glow, the Delivery tile and the CTA gradient keep the old violet.

findings.message: `disallow: "/"` with an allow-list that leaves out `/icon.svg` (the new favicon) and `/signin` (the public page's only links besides anchors). Crawlers can't fetch the site icon shown in search results. Add `/icon.svg` to the allow list.
findings.scenario: Googlebot fetches /icon.svg → it is blocked by robots.txt, and search results show a generic icon.
